title: Bayan Fingerprint v1
description: A per-response diagnostic record emitted inside a deployment boundary. Every property carries x-bayan-tier, a sensitivity level from 0 (vendor artefact, no client derivation) to 4 (content, never present in a fingerprint). Projection to tier m retains only properties whose tier is <= m, plus the always-retained set listed in x-bayan-always. Tier NAMES are supplied by the deployment's policy profile and are deliberately absent from this schema (PRD R-2.1).

x-bayan-tier-scale.0: Vendor artefact. Not derived from client data. Always releasable.
x-bayan-tier-scale.1: Operational. Client-derived but non-identifying in isolation.
x-bayan-tier-scale.2: Structural. Client-derived; safe only in aggregate or under pseudonymisation.
x-bayan-tier-scale.3: Sensitive inference. Protected inference about an identifiable subject.
x-bayan-tier-scale.4: Content. Never carried in a fingerprint; reference only.

recordId.description: ULID. Opaque, monotonic, vendor-generated, carries no client semantics. Tier 0 because it is in x-bayan-always: an always-retained field cannot be tiered above the lowest projection target.

classification.description: Travels with every record and every projection. PRD R-P4, R-P5.

scheme.description: Identifier of the client's own classification scheme. Bayan never imposes its own labels.

tier.description: A label from that scheme, verbatim.

sensitivity.description: The scheme tier mapped onto the 0-4 scale by the policy profile. Used for projection.

indexVersion.description: Container at tier 1 so `generation` survives a low projection; the DIGEST is tier 2. The retrieval index is built from the CLIENT's corpus, so its digest is client-derived and a changing value leaks corpus-mutation timing (PRD 2.2 B6). Where timing is itself sensitive, emit generation only.

route.description: Enumerated pipeline path. Closed set declared per product; free text is invalid.

errorCode.description: Closed enumeration. Free text is invalid by construction: error strings routinely embed the user content that failed to parse (PRD R-F3, NIST AC-4(14)).

ms.description: Exact latency. Combined with token counts this reconstructs message shape (PRD 2.2 B6).

coarse.description: Truncated to the granularity the profile sets. Default: hour.

conversationId.description: HMAC-SHA256 under an enclave-resident key. Stable within a deployment, unlinkable across deployments.

docRefs.description: Pseudonymised document identifiers (PRD R-F5). A SEQUENCE of real doc IDs reconstructs what a user was reading; in a small corpus the ID is the content. Each entry must be HMAC'd under an enclave-resident key and must satisfy the profile's k-frequency floor. Entries below the floor are dropped, not included with a flag.

categories.description: The most sensitive field in this schema (PRD 2.2 B6, R-F6). A category name is a protected inference about an identifiable subject at a known time, generated by the vendor's own system. Non-exportable in the default profile; releasable only as cohort counts above a k-floor.

confidence.description: A per-record confidence score is an inference about a specific interaction and is treated as sensitive.

names.description: Which tool was invoked can reveal the nature of the request.

contentRef.description: A POINTER to the separately-stored prompt/response content, never the content itself. The referent is tier 4 and never travels in a fingerprint. Mirrors the OTel split between the span and OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_UPLOAD_BASE_PATH.

pseudonym.description: Lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 output. The key never leaves the enclave.

x-bayan-invariants: A property listed in x-bayan-always must have x-bayan-tier 0.
A required property must have x-bayan-tier 0, or a tier-0 projection is unconstructable.
A container's tier must be <= the minimum tier of its children, or low-tier children become unreachable by projection.
Projection is monotonic: the field set retained at tier n is a subset of that retained at tier n+1.
Projection is lossy by omission only. It never transforms a value.
